hindi: हे मरुतों के पिता, तुम्हारी कृपा हमारे पास आए; हमें सूर्य के दर्शन से अलग न करो। हमारा वीर घोड़े के सामने टिका रहे; हे रुद्र, हम संतान के साथ बढ़ें।
english: O father of the Maruts, may your favour come to us; do not separate us from the sight of the sun. May our hero hold out against the charger; O Rudra, may we be born forth with offspring.
notes: 'abhi ... arvati kṣameta' is uncertain: arvati is taken as locative of arvant 'charger', abhi as 'against'; the sense 'hold out against the charger' is a literal guess. 'pra jāyemahi' is literally 'may we be born forth'.

hindi: हे रुद्र, तुम्हारे दिए हुए अत्यंत सुखकर उपचारों के साथ मैं सौ वर्ष पाऊँ। हमसे द्वेष को दूर करो, और भी दूर करो; संकट को दूर करो; पीड़ाओं को बिखेरकर दूर भगाओ।
english: O Rudra, with the most beneficial remedies given by you, may I attain a hundred winters. Drive hatred away from us, further away; drive away distress; drive off the afflictions, scattering them in all directions.

text_flags.why: possible stray digit 1 after 'vya' (accent or footnote mark); the word is vi asmat dveṣaḥ

notes: 'viṣūcīḥ' is taken as 'in different directions', agreeing with amīvāḥ. 'amīvā' is rendered 'affliction' (literally something that afflicts).

hindi: हे रुद्र, तुम उत्पन्न हुओं में तेज से सर्वश्रेष्ठ हो, बलवानों में सबसे बलवान हो, हे वज्र भुजाओं वाले। हमें संकट के पार ले चलो; कल्याण दो; हानि के सब आक्रमणों को दूर रखो।
english: O Rudra, you are the best of the born in splendour, the mightiest of the mighty, O thunderbolt-armed one. Carry us across to the far side of distress; grant well-being; keep away all assaults of harm.
notes: 'abhītī rapasaḥ' is abhītīḥ rapasaḥ by ordinary sandhi (īḥ r- gives ī r-). 'svasti' is taken with the sense 'well-being' as the object of the imperative; the line is elliptical. 'rapas' rendered 'harm'.

hindi: हे रुद्र, हम तुम्हें प्रणामों से क्रुद्ध न करें, न बुरी स्तुति से, हे वृषभ, न सम्मिलित पुकार से। उपचारों से हमारे वीरों को उठाओ; वैद्यों में तुम्हें सर्वश्रेष्ठ वैद्य सुनता हूँ।
english: O Rudra, may we not anger you with obeisances, nor with ill praise, O bull, nor with joint invocation. Raise up our heroes with remedies; I hear you to be the best physician of physicians.
notes: The first half is uncertain in construction: 'namobhiḥ' (obeisances) as the means of angering is taken literally, in the sense of obeisances wrongly offered; 'sahūtī' (joint invocation) is taken literally. 'śṛṇomi' with accusative 'tvā' is rendered 'I hear (that you are)'; the translation keeps 'hear you to be'.

hindi: जो पुकारों से, हवियों से बुलाया जाता है, उस रुद्र को मैं स्तुतियों से प्रसन्न करूँ। कोमल पेट वाला, सरलता से बुलाया जाने वाला, भूरा, सुंदर ओठों वाला वह हमें इस द्वेष के हाथ न सौंपे।
english: Rudra, who is invoked with cries and with oblations, may I appease with praises. Soft-bellied, easy to invoke, tawny, fair-lipped, may he not give us over to this ill will.
notes: 'ava diṣīya' is uncertain: taken as an optative meaning 'may I appease' (ava with a root meaning to bind or appease). 'su-śipra' is rendered 'fair-lipped' (some take it as 'fair-helmeted'). 'manāyai' is uncertain: taken as 'ill will'. 'ṛdūdara' literally 'soft-bellied'.

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pres. part. mid. √nādh

hindi: मरुतों से युक्त वृषभ ने मुझ याचना करने वाले को अधिक बलवान जीवन-शक्ति से प्रसन्न किया है। जैसे ताप से पीड़ित छाया को, वैसे निर्दोष होकर मैं उसे पाऊँ; मैं रुद्र की कृपा को सेवा से पाऊँ।
english: The bull accompanied by the Maruts has gladdened me, who beg, with more vigorous life force. Like one in the heat reaching shade, free from fault may I attain it; may I win Rudra's favour by service.

text_flags.why: double apostrophe after the word looks like a stray mark or an avagraha artefact; the word is aśīya

notes: 'ghṛṇīva chāyām' is read ghṛṇiḥ iva chāyām 'like one in the heat (seeking) shade'; the object of aśīya is not stated, so the translation completes only what the grammar needs. 'vivāseyam' (root vas, 'serve, honour') is uncertain. nādhamāna 'one in need, begging' is taken from √nādh.

hindi: हे रुद्र, तुम्हारा वह कृपालु हाथ कहाँ है जो उपचार करने वाला और शीतल करने वाला है? हे वृषभ, तुम देवों की हानि को दूर करने वाले हो; अब मुझे क्षमा करो।
english: Where is that gracious hand of yours, O Rudra, which is healing and soothing? Remover of the harm of the gods, O bull, now pardon me.

text_flags.why: stray digit 1 after 'kva' (accent or footnote mark)

notes: 'jalāṣa' is traditionally 'soothing, cooling'; rendered 'soothing' but uncertain. 'daivyasya rapasaḥ' is rendered 'harm of the gods' (harm coming from the gods is a possible reading). 'abhi ... cakṣamīthāḥ' is taken as 'pardon', form uncertain.

words.gram: 2 sg. imv. (or f. inst. sg. 'with homage', uncertain)

hindi: महान् भूरे वृषभ, उज्ज्वल रूप वाले के लिए मैं महान् उत्तम स्तुति भेजता हूँ। उस दीप्तिमान् को प्रणाम करो; प्रणामों के साथ हम रुद्र के प्रचंड नाम की स्तुति करते हैं।
english: To the tawny bull, the bright one, I send forth a great good praise. Do homage to the blazing one; with obeisances we praise the fierce name of Rudra.
notes: 'śvitīce' (bright, white) and 'kalmalīkinam' (blazing) are uncertain; 'maho' is taken as an agreeing dative 'great' but the form is unclear. 'namasyā' may be an imperative 'do homage' or an instrumental 'with homage'; in the latter case the line would read 'we praise the blazing one with homage, with obeisances the fierce name of Rudra'.

hindi: दृढ़ अंगों से, अनेक रूपों वाला, प्रचंड, भूरा, वह चमकते सोने के आभूषणों से सजा है। इस विशाल जगत् के स्वामी रुद्र से प्रभुत्व कभी अलग नहीं होगा।
english: With firm limbs, of many forms, mighty, tawny, he is adorned with bright gold. Lordship, asurya, will not indeed separate from Rudra, the ruler of this abundant world.
notes: 'īśānād ... rudrād' both ablatives; the translation takes 'īśānāt' in apposition to Rudra ('from Rudra, the ruler'), a literal reading. 'asurya' is rendered 'lordship' with the Sanskrit given. 'pipiśe' is taken as 'is adorned'.

hindi: योग्य होकर तुम बाण और धनुष धारण करते हो; योग्य होकर पूजनीय, सब रूपों वाला निष्क धारण करते हो। योग्य होकर तुम इस सारे विशाल पर दया करते हो; हे रुद्र, तुमसे बढ़कर बलवान् कोई नहीं।
english: Worthy, you bear arrows and a bow; worthy, a venerable niṣka of every form. Worthy, you show mercy to all this immensity; none indeed is mightier than you, O Rudra.
notes: 'arhan' is rendered 'worthy' (as is fitting). 'niṣka' is a gold neck ornament; kept as niṣka. 'dayase' (mercy, or apportioning) and 'abhva' (immense, monstrous; here a noun) are uncertain.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. pass.

hindi: प्रसिद्ध, रथ के आसन पर बैठने वाले, युवा, जंगली पशु के समान भयंकर, निकट से प्रहार करने वाले, प्रचंड रुद्र की स्तुति करो। हे रुद्र, स्तुति पाकर गायक पर कृपा करो; तुम्हारी सेनाएँ हमारे सिवा किसी और को काट गिराएँ।
english: Praise the renowned one, who sits in the chariot seat, the youth, terrible like a wild beast, the smiter close at hand, the mighty. O Rudra, being praised, be gracious to the singer; let your hosts cut down another than us.
notes: 'gartasad' is taken as 'sitting in the chariot seat' (garta, a seat or cavity). The name Rudra is not in the first line; the object of 'stuhi' is the described one. 'anyam te asmat ni vapantu' is literally 'let your hosts cut down another, away from us'.

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pres. part. mid. √vand (or: greeting)
m. acc. sg. pres. part. upa-√i

hindi: हे रुद्र, मैं तुम्हारे पास आते हुए की ओर झुका हूँ, जैसे बालक भी अभिवादन किए जाते पिता की ओर झुकता है। प्रचुरता के दाता, सज्जनों के स्वामी की मैं स्तुति करता हूँ; स्तुति पाकर तुम हमें उपचार दो।
english: I have bowed towards you, O Rudra, as you approach, as even a boy bows towards his father who is being greeted. I praise you, the giver of abundance, lord of the good; praised, give us remedies.
notes: Construction of the first line is uncertain: 'kumāraś cit pitaraṃ vandamānam' (a boy bowing to, or greeting, his father) is taken as an implied comparison, and 'prati nānāma ... upayantam' as 'I bowed towards you as you approach'; there is no explicit word for 'as'. 'gṛṇīṣe' person (1 sg. mid. or a 2 sg. passive) and 'rāsi' (a rare imperative form) are uncertain.

hindi: हे मरुतो, तुम्हारे जो शुद्ध उपचार हैं, हे वृषभो, जो अत्यंत सुखकर हैं, जो आरामदायक हैं, जिन्हें हमारे पिता मनु ने चुना, उन्हें, और रुद्र के कल्याण तथा रक्षण को मैं चाहता हूँ।
english: Your remedies, O Maruts, that are pure, that are most beneficial, O bulls, that are comforting, those that Manu, our father, chose, those I desire, and the blessing and protection of Rudra.
notes: 'śam ca yoś ca' is a fixed pair, rendered 'blessing and protection'. 'rudrasya' may be read 'from Rudra'. The sentence is elliptical: 'tā' and 'śaṃ ca yoś ca' are both objects of 'vaśmi'.

hindi: रुद्र का शस्त्र हमसे बचकर निकल जाए; उस प्रचंड की महान् दुर्भावना हमारे पास से गुज़र जाए। हे उदार, उदार दाताओं के लिए दृढ़ वस्तुओं को ढीला करो; संतान और वंशज पर कृपा करो।
english: May the missile of Rudra be turned aside from us; may the great ill will of the fierce one pass us by. Slacken the firm ones for the generous patrons; O bountiful one, be gracious to child and descendant.
notes: 'sthirā' is neuter plural 'firm ones'; the noun is not stated (some take it as the bows). 'hetī' is hetiḥ by sandhi (iḥ r- gives ī r-); the visarga forms 'vṛjyāḥ' and 'durmatiḥ mahī' are read as printed.

hindi: इसी प्रकार, हे भूरे वृषभ, हे सजग देव, जिससे तुम न क्रुद्ध हो और न प्रहार करो। हे पुकार सुनने वाले रुद्र, यहाँ हमारी ओर ध्यान दो; हम उत्तम वीरों से युक्त होकर यज्ञ में ऊँचे स्वर से बोलें।
english: So, O tawny bull, O attentive god, that you may neither be angry nor strike. Hearer of invocations, O Rudra, take heed of us here; may we speak greatly at the rite, rich in heroes.
notes: 'bṛhad vadema' is the refrain of this hymn group; 'bṛhat' is literally 'great', rendered 'greatly' (often taken as 'loudly'). The first line is a purpose clause that depends on a verb not stated in it.
